stories.title: Investment and Advisory Platform Leases Full Floor at 545 Madison
stories.excerpt: Marx Realty announced that Patricof Co, a specialized investment and advisory platform serving professional athletes, has signed a 10-year lease at 545 Madison. At the Plaza District office building, the firm will occupy 7,500 square feet comprising the entire 16th floor. “Patricof’s move to 545 Madison speaks to the high quality of tenants that are attracted to the distinctive design of the building as firms are drawn to the elevated ecosystem at this building,” said Craig Deitelzweig, president and CEO of Marx Realty. “The intentional design details and sophisticated warmth create a hospitality-infused sensibility that appeals to top-tier firms, and we are delighted to welcome Patricof as it grows in a new location to 545 Madison.”  Chase Gordon and Luke Dillmeier of Transwestern represented Patricof. Marx Realty was represented by Tara Stacom, Peter Trivelas, Harry Blair, and Remy Leibersohn of Cushman & Wakefield. The post Investment and Advisory Platform Leases Full Floor at 545 Madison appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Patricof Co. leases 7,500 sq ft (entire 16th floor) at 545 Madison, NYC office.
10-year lease signals continued high-quality tenant demand in Plaza District.
No direct multifamily demand or supply signal; office-focused transaction.
stories.summary: Patricof Co., an investment and advisory platform serving professional athletes, signed a 10-year lease for 7,500 square feet at 545 Madison in New York's Plaza District. The deal reflects ongoing demand from tier-one firms for premium office space in well-designed buildings. Marx Realty emphasized the building's 'elevated ecosystem' and design quality as drivers of tenant attraction.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing strength in Midtown Manhattan does not materially affect apartment demand, supply, or financing in the metro. No second-order effect on residential markets.

stories.title: Faris Lee Arranges $39M Deal for Big-Box Duo within Lakewood Center
stories.excerpt: Faris Lee Investments completed the $38.7-million acquisition of a 155,000-square-foot, two-tenant retail investment featuring The Home Depot and Albertsons at Lakewood Center in Lakewood. Managing principals Don MacLellan and Jeff Conover, senior managing director Scott DeYoung and director Greg Lukosky represented the seller, a consortium of multiple owners, as well as the buyer, a high-net-worth family office. The property encompasses approximately 154,997 square feet on 14.7 acres within Lakewood Center, a dominant regional retail destination serving a densely populated trade area in Los Angeles County. Both Home Depot and Albertsons occupy their respective parcels under absolute below-market ground leases. “Transactions of this caliber require a deep understanding of both the real estate and the investment objectives of the buyer,” said MacLellan. “Lakewood Center is an exceptional retail destination, and the opportunity to acquire two dominant national tenants in such a supply-constrained Southern California location is extremely compelling.” The post Faris Lee Arranges $39M Deal for Big-Box Duo within Lakewood Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Faris Lee acquires $38.7M retail center (Home Depot, Albertsons) in Lakewood, CA.
155,000 sq ft on 14.7 acres; tenants on below-market ground leases.
Supply-constrained SoCal retail market; family office capital active in anchored retail.
stories.summary: A high-net-worth family office, represented by Faris Lee Investments, acquired a 155,000-square-foot retail property anchored by Home Depot and Albertsons at Lakewood Center in Los Angeles County for $38.7 million. Both tenants occupy parcels under absolute below-market ground leases. The deal highlights the appeal of dominant national retailers and long-term lease stability in supply-constrained Southern California.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily signal. However, the deal underscores robust family office capital deployment into real estate and strong retail fundamentals in dense LA County submarkets. If capital continues flowing to retail, it may compete with multifamily for land and development equity in supply-constrained Southern California markets. Lakewood's density and trade area support both retail and residential demand.

stories.title: Stockbridge Buys Maryland Industrial Property for $57M
stories.excerpt: Stockbridge has acquired a 203,000-square-foot industrial property in Maryland for $56.6 million, almost four years after seller TA Realty bought the facility for about the same price. The San Francisco-based investment management firm purchased the Class A building at 8511 Pepco Place in Upper Marlboro, Md., according to Cushman & Wakefield, which represented the seller. CoStar first reported the news. The 13-acre property is fully leased to Harris Company, a mechanical contractor that has become a major service provider to hyperscale data center operators. Harris first occupied about 34 percent of the building before recently expanding to fill the entire space. The facility was built in 2008 about half a mile east of the Capital Beltway and near Joint Base Andrews. It includes a 190-foot truck court, 26 dock doors, two drive-in doors, 218 parking spaces and roughly 75 trailer spots. TA Realty acquired the asset from an affiliate of electrical distributor Sonepar in 2022 for $56.2 million. Harris’ expansion comes as Greater Washington’s data center industry drives demand for industrial space tied to construction, infrastructure and operations. Cushman & Wakefield’s Jonathan Carpenter, Graham Savage, Dawes Milchling and James Check worked on the transaction. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Stockbridge acquires 203,000 sq ft industrial in Upper Marlboro, MD for $56.6M.
Tenant: Harris Company (mechanical contractor serving hyperscale data centers); fully leased.
Near Capital Beltway and Joint Base Andrews; built 2008; flat pricing vs. 2022.
stories.summary: Stockbridge acquired a fully leased 203,000-square-foot Class A industrial property at 8511 Pepco Place in Upper Marlboro, Maryland for $56.6 million. The sole tenant, Harris Company, a mechanical contractor serving hyperscale data center operators, recently expanded to occupy the entire facility. The property, built in 2008 and located near the Capital Beltway and Joint Base Andrews, was acquired by seller TA Realty for approximately the same price in 2022.
stories.impact: Signals strong demand for industrial space serving data center supply chains in Maryland's industrial corridor. Data center construction and operations will drive continued job growth and population influx into the DC metro region, particularly in submarkets near fiber routes and major operators. This supports sustained multifamily demand across Northern Virginia, Maryland, and DC proper; multifamily developers should monitor data center announcements and expansions (especially Ashburn, Sterling, Upper Marlboro areas) as leading indicators of near-term rental demand.

stories.title: Net Lease: From Niche to Institutional Strategy
stories.excerpt: Net lease investment was once the purview of private investors and buyers completing 1031 exchanges. Not anymore. According to a recent Northmarq article, net lease sales have evolved from a small part of commercial real estate into a bona fide institutional investment strategy. In the News Two September announcements highlight the interest shown by the “bigger players” in net lease investments. J.P. Morgan Asset Management closed its inaugural U.S. net lease fund with $1.1 billion in commitments, which was more than twice its original $500 million target. The fund focuses on single-tenant industrial and outdoor storage properties with long-term, triple-net leases. U.S. private equity firm Cerberus sold real estate finance company Tenet Equity to CBRE Investment Management. The portfolio includes 208 net lease assets totaling approximately 12 million square feet. The move paved the way for the buyer to pursue additional investments in sale-leaseback transactions. While the announcements don’t suddenly put net lease into the spotlight, Northmarq said they demonstrate that “large investors are allocating capital to dedicated strategies, acquiring established platforms and pairing real estate analysis with corporate-credit underwriting.” The Net Lease Attraction Industrial properties have been important to the expansion. Research indicated approximately $13.5 billion in single-tenant investment sales during Q2 2026, a 19.1% increase from the year before. Industrial accounted for $8.4 billion, or nearly two-thirds of the total. Institutional investors also increased their share of acquisitions year over year. Northmarq also said that the market is more than just the buying and selling of individual properties, including healthcare facilities, corporate locations and additional operational real estate. At the same time, investors might “pursue individual acquisitions, programmatic ventures or dedicated fund strategies,” Northmarq said. What it Means A larger capital base
bullets: J.P. Morgan Asset Management closed $1.1B inaugural net lease fund; 2x original target.
Cerberus sold Tenet Equity (208 assets, 12M sq ft NTL) to CBRE Investment Management.
Institutional capital now dedicated to single-tenant industrial and outdoor storage with long-term leases.
stories.summary: Institutional investors are rapidly professionalizing net lease strategy. J.P. Morgan Asset Management's inaugural U.S. net lease fund closed at $1.1 billion in commitments—more than double its $500 million target—focusing on single-tenant industrial and outdoor storage with long-term, triple-net leases. Simultaneously, Cerberus sold real estate finance platform Tenet Equity (208 net lease assets, ~12M sq ft) to CBRE Investment Management, enabling broader sale-leaseback investing.
stories.impact: Institutional capital consolidation in net lease reduces available equity for development and sale-leaseback opportunities; cap rates may compress further, crimping risk-adjusted returns on single-tenant strategies. For multifamily developers, this signals that large pools of capital are locked into long-duration, low-volatility industrial and outdoor storage—not residential. However, if institutional net lease funds expand into multifamily (rare but possible), it could signal a flight to yield and operational stability post-rate volatility. Monitor CBRE Investment Management and J.P. Morgan for any residential allocations.

stories.title: Inside Ken Griffin’s $3B Bet on Miami’s Wynwood
stories.excerpt: Three years ago, staffers working for billionaire financier Ken Griffin met with Moishe Mana to present him the deal of lifetime: They offered about $800 million for his 35-acre portfolio in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood. Surprised, Mana initially rejected the offer. His properties were not for sale, and he envisioned developing his own business and entertainment district. But three days later, the investor relented. “Once I understood that this is going to be good for Miami,” Mana explained at a press event Thursday. “It’s completing our vision, not competing. I said, ‘Let’s go.’” The cash deal, which ultimately ballooned to $1.1 billion, closed this week without any outside debt and partners for Griffin. It marked one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in the country’s history. What’s more: Griffin pledged an additional $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, bringing his total giving to $3 billion — the largest combined donation to higher education from a private individual. $1 billion of the gift will support the university’s Pittsburgh campus, while $2 billion will support the launch of CMU Miami and includes the value of the real estate. The gift will help address one of Miami’s biggest challenges as it seeks to become a global business hub: its lack of top-tier universities, which are crucial to create a pipeline of employable grads for tech and finance companies. “If you look at Pittsburgh and the economic renaissance taking place: 250 tech startups, 100 companies focused on robotics,” Griffin said during a public address Thursday. “The future of America is being built in Pittsburgh — that future will be strengthened by what we build in Miami.” The Wynwood campus is expected to house more than 3,500 undergraduates, master’s, and PhD students as well as nearly 300 faculty members, and more than 600 staff. bullets: Ken Griffin acquires Moishe Mana's 35-acre Wynwood portfolio for $1.1B (closed this week).

Miami Wynwood positioned for mixed-use redevelopment; major capital infusion into downtown regeneration.
stories.summary: Billionaire Ken Griffin closed a $1.1 billion all-cash acquisition of Moishe Mana's 35-acre portfolio in Miami's Wynwood neighborhood. Griffin simultaneously pledged $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University (total giving: $3 billion), signaling deep commitment to Miami's development future. The deal—one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in U.S. history—was completed without external debt or partners, positioning Wynwood for major mixed-use redevelopment.
stories.impact: MAJOR DEMAND AND CAPITAL SIGNAL FOR SOUTH FLORIDA. Griffin's $1.1B Wynwood acquisition and $3B total commitment indicate sustained confidence in Miami's growth trajectory and willingness to deploy patient, equity capital into neighborhood transformation. Wynwood's 35 acres will likely be repositioned for residential, retail, hospitality, and office mixed-use. This signals strong multifamily demand in the Miami metro and potential for rent growth in Wynwood and adjacent downtown neighborhoods. Multifamily developers should aggressively underwrite ground-up or conversion projects in Wynwood, Allapattah, and Edgewater; Griffin's capital deployment validates these submarkets and may accelerate in-migration and job growth. Watch for Griffin's development timeline and anchor tenants (especially tech, finance, or corporate relocations) to gauge pipeline timing.

stories.title: Malaysian Bank, Medical Practice Sign Leases at 575 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: A Malaysian bank and a concierge medical service together took more than 14,100 square feet of office space in Midtown. Malayan Banking Berhad, also known as Maybank, signed the largest of the two deals with 8,629 square feet across the entire 24th floor of Steinberg & Pokoik Management’s 575 Madison Avenue, according to landlord broker CBRE. CBRE did not disclose the asking rent, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the third quarter of 2026 was $85.08 per square foot, according to a report from Colliers. Maybank will relocate its New York City offices from 400 Park Avenue about three blocks away. Meanwhile, the smaller of the two deals was for Park 55 Medical Associates, where Dr. Wendy Ziecheck and Dr. Christopher Barley will practice medicine. Park 55 leased 5,474 square feet on part of the 10th and 15th floors of the building. “575 Madison Avenue attracts leading financial services and professional services tenants seeking a prestigious address and exceptional building amenities,” CBRE’s Gregg Rothkin said in a statement. “These latest transactions underscore the demand for high-quality office space in a premier Midtown location.” Rothkin negotiated on behalf of the landlord alongside CBRE’s David Hollander, Brad Auerbach, Maxwell Tarter and William Hooks, but it’s unclear who represented the tenants in the deals. In a third deal, another concierge health clinic, which CBRE declined to identify, leased 14,211 square feet at 575 Madison, according to the brokerage. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Maybank (Malaysia) leases 8,629 sq ft (24th floor) at 575 Madison; relocated from 400 Park Ave.
Park 55 Medical Associates leases 5,474 sq ft across 10th/15th floors.

stories.summary: Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) signed the larger of two deals, taking 8,629 square feet on the entire 24th floor of 575 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, relocating from 400 Park Avenue. Park 55 Medical Associates leased 5,474 square feet across two floors. Both deals reflect ongoing demand for premium office in Midtown; Q3 2026 asking rent averaged $85.08/sq ft.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily signal. Midtown office demand and rental rates do not materially affect apartment markets. Maybank's short three-block relocation and medical practice leasing show resilience in high-end Manhattan office but do not indicate broader downtown residential demand shifts. No secondary effect on multifamily.

stories.title: Helaba Provides $105M Construction Takeout Loan on Nashville Apartments
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential has secured $105 million of construction takeout financing for a newly built mixed-use project in Nashville, Commercial Observer has learned. German commercial bank Helaba supplied the bridge loan for the sponsorship’s Modera Riverview development that debuted in 2024 in Nashville’s Germantown neighborhood. PNC previously provided a $103 million construction loan for the 400-unit property, which also features 13,998 square feet of retail space. Located at 1410 Adams Street, off the west shore of the Cumberland River two miles north of Downtown Nashville, Modera Riverview has resident amenities that include a swimming pool, a rooftop lounge, a fitness center, coworking spaces and a golf simulator. The ground-floor retail space is 100 percent leased to Legacy Fitness and Italian restaurant Indaco. Jason Deck, director of real estate finance at Helaba, said having two “highly experienced multifamily operators” and a property in a city with strong momentum made the deal attractive. “Nashville continues to perform well and remains an important market for our U.S. real estate platform,” Deck said in a statement. CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Helaba provides $105M construction takeout for Modera Riverview, Nashville (400 units, 14K retail).
CrossHarbor/Mill Creek JV; delivered 2024 in Germantown; PNC originally provided $103M construction loan.
Ground-floor retail 100% leased (Legacy Fitness, Indaco restaurant); strong Nashville momentum cited.
stories.summary: A joint venture between CrossHarbor Capital Partners and Mill Creek Residential secured $105 million of construction takeout financing from German bank Helaba for Modera Riverview, a 400-unit mixed-use development in Nashville's Germantown neighborhood delivered in 2024. Ground-floor retail (14,000 sq ft) is fully leased to Legacy Fitness and Italian restaurant Indaco. PNC originally provided the $103 million construction loan.
stories.impact: POSITIVE MULTIFAMILY SIGNAL FOR NASHVILLE. Helaba's willingness to provide takeout financing at parity to construction loan ($105M vs. $103M) signals confidence in Nashville's rental market and operator strength. Mill Creek's presence and strong leasing metrics (full ground-floor retail, premium amenities) validate Germantown as a core multifamily submarket. The deal indicates lender comfort with Nashville's job and population growth, particularly around downtown riverfront. Multifamily developers should prioritize Germantown, Nations, and east-of-downtown corridors where job centers (healthcare, tech, finance) are concentrating. Watch for continued capital deployment by institutional operators like Mill Creek and CrossHarbor; they are leading indicators of multifamily demand velocity.

stories.title: Joyland Sells Staten Island Shopping Center for $57M
stories.excerpt: South Shore Commons, a popular shopping and dining plaza on Staten Island, has sold for the second time in four years. Joyland Management sold the 157,347-square-foot outdoor shopping center at 2965 Veterans Road West for $57 million, or $362 per square foot, to real estate investment trust Phillips Edison & Company, which owns and manages grocery-anchored shopping centers across the U.S. A source with knowledge of the deal confirmed the transaction. Traded first reported the deal. Spokespeople for the buyer and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Joel Wertzberger, Judy Wolcowitz and Jack Wolcowitz of Joyland Management handled the sale in-house, while Newmark’s Daniel O’Brien, Conor Lalor, Caroline Hodes, Loren Valla, Felton Hatcher and Adam Spies represented the seller and procured the buyer. Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Jack Wolcowitz bought South Shore Commons in 2022 for an undisclosed amount. Joyland refinanced the property in 2023 for $41.8 million. The property changed hands before that in 2018 for $41 million. The tenant roster at South Shore Commons includes Filoncino Bakery Cafe, Dunkin, Pronto Pizza, Sola Salon Studios, Retro Fitness and Sally Beauty. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Joyland Management sells South Shore Commons (Staten Island) to Phillips Edison for $57M.
157,347 sq ft grocery-anchored center; $362/sq ft; second sale in four years.
Joyland acquired 2022, refinanced 2023 for $41.8M; quick turnaround with capital gains.
stories.summary: Joyland Management sold South Shore Commons, a 157,347-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center at 2965 Veterans Road West in Staten Island, to REIT Phillips Edison & Company for $57 million ($362/sq ft). Joyland had acquired the property in 2022 and refinanced it for $41.8 million in 2023, indicating a profitable exit. This marks the second transaction for the center in four years.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, strong appetite from grocery-anchored REIT Phillips Edison signals robust retail fundamentals and landlord confidence in Staten Island's suburban demographic stability. If retail capital is anchoring to grocery and outparcel tenants in outer boroughs, it reflects sustained neighborhood demand and affordability. This indirectly supports multifamily fundamentals in Staten Island by validating population retention and local spending power, but does not drive new apartment supply or demand signals. No secondary effect on development pipeline.
